\chapter{More Everyday Verbs}
\label{ch:sa-more-verbs}
\hlchaptermodality{21}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone drinks, laughs, stands and remembers in Sanskrit.}

Complete SA-C21-remember and say all four verbs in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[nṛtyati]{\sk{नृत्यति} (nṛtyati) — he, she or it dances}

\label{lesson:SA-C21-dance}



\begin{quote}
A short run of everyday verbs, one at a time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{नृत्यति}}
\textbf{\sk{नृत्यति}} (\emph{nṛtyati}) — \textquotedblleft{}he, she or it dances\textquotedblright{}.

From \textbf{√\sk{नृत्}} (\emph{nṛt}), 'to dance'. It gives \emph{nṛtya}, the danced half of the classical performing arts, as against \emph{nāṭya}, the acted half — a distinction Sanskrit draws that English does not.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nṛtyati}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{नृत्यति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}he, she or it dances\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hasati]{\sk{हसति} (hasati) — he, she or it laughs}

\label{lesson:SA-C21-laugh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{nṛtyati} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{हसति}}
\textbf{\sk{हसति}} (\emph{hasati}) — \textquotedblleft{}he, she or it laughs\textquotedblright{}.

From \textbf{√\sk{हस्}} (\emph{has}). It is the word inside \emph{hāsya}, the comic mood in the classical theory of drama — one of the nine \emph{rasas}, so laughter here is a category of art, not only a noise.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{hasati}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{nṛtyati}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{हसति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}he, she or it laughs\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tiṣṭhati]{\sk{तिष्ठति} (tiṣṭhati) — he, she or it stands}

\label{lesson:SA-C21-stand}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{hasati} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{तिष्ठति}}
\textbf{\sk{तिष्ठति}} (\emph{tiṣṭhati}) — \textquotedblleft{}he, she or it stands\textquotedblright{}.

From \textbf{√\sk{स्था}} (\emph{sthā}), 'to stand' — the same root as Latin \emph{stare} and English \textbf{stand}, \textbf{stable}, \textbf{status}. The \emph{ti-} at the front is reduplication again, exactly as in \emph{nṛtyati}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. Three more follow, and each reuses the ones before it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{tiṣṭhati}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{hasati}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{तिष्ठति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}he, she or it stands\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[smarati]{\sk{स्मरति} (smarati) — he, she or it remembers}

\label{lesson:SA-C21-remember}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{tiṣṭhati} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{स्मरति}}
\textbf{\sk{स्मरति}} (\emph{smarati}) — \textquotedblleft{}he, she or it remembers\textquotedblright{}.

From \textbf{√\sk{स्मृ}} (\emph{smṛ}), 'to remember'. It gives \emph{smṛti}, 'that which is remembered' — the name for a whole class of texts, as against \emph{śruti}, 'that which is heard'. A memory word doing bibliographic work.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more everyday action. That closes the run: four everyday actions, each met on its own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{smarati}
  \item it again, to someone standing in a doorway
  \item it after \emph{tiṣṭhati}, so the two sit together
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \sk{स्मरति} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}he, she or it remembers\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
